limitations: All source roots are disposable pytest fixtures on the existing host, not an immutable APFS snapshot or single T view.

Tree membership, metadata, symlink targets, and included bytes are compared sequentially through held no-follow descriptors; this does not prevent or characterize all concurrent mutation of a live source.

The SQLite source-family pass compares post-backup receipt lstat signatures for DB/WAL/SHM/journal names. It does not read or hash their contents and does not prove that the backup corresponds to a snapshot source point.
Fixture setup separately creates the SQLite online backup from its disposable synthetic DB, so the whole rehearsal logically reads that synthetic database.
Snapshot identity, durable cutoff, policy/tool attestations, and event timestamps remain declared synthetic fields.
The protected root is only verified as an opaque captured artifact; it is not source-bound. One excluded descendant remains unresolved, so full owner root closure is not claimed.
Metadata parity does not qualify restore xattrs/ACLs/flags or host ownership mapping. No clean-host restore or erase readiness is established.
